# Board Game Night Planner

Curated by Skill Harbor — plans game nights that actually work: it matches games and their running order to your group — player count, experience levels, available time, game complexity, and social energy — so the night flows instead of stalling on a rules explanation nobody finishes. It handles the sequencing problem (warm-up game first, the heavy one in the middle, something light to close), teaches-what-fits-first thinking, and the practical logistics of table time and teaching overhead. Discovered via skills.sh, listed here with credit to its creator by @mohitagw15856. Honest caveats: a planning discipline, no code and no game database — it reasons from the games you own or name, it doesn't know your shelf; it can't fix a group that really wanted to play video games; its plans assume you teach rules honestly — budget the teaching time it suggests. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Not verified.
